title: A Phase III, Multicenter, Randomized, Controlled, Double-Blind Study Comparing the Efficacy and Safety of Test Product versus Standard Local Anesthesia in Transurethral Procedures
official: A Phase III, Multicenter, Randomized, Controlled, Double-Blind Study Comparing the Efficacy and Safety of High-Dose (4%) versus Standard (2%) Lidocaine Gel for Local Anesthesia in Transurethral Procedures
summary: Main objective: To demonstrate the superiority of the test product versus comperator in reducing the intraoperative pain intensity during placement or exchange of DJ ureteral stent.
conditions: Placement or exchange of double-J (DJ) ureteral stent
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Freely given written informed consent prior to any study-specific procedure.
2. Male or female participant ≥18 years old, at the time of signing the informed consent.
3. Patients scheduled for placement or exchange of a DJ ureteral stent.
4. Willingness to accept and comply with all study procedures and restrictions.
5. A female participant is eligible if she meets one of the following criteria: a) is of non-childbearing potential; or b) is of childbearing potential and agrees to use an accepted contraceptive method from Screening until the EoS.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Known hypersensitivity/allergic reaction to lidocaine or any other anaesthetics of the amide type.
2. Known defects in the lower urinary tract, including but not limited to urethral strictures.
3. Use of any medication or substance that may interfere with pain perception, sedation, dizziness, cognition, procedural tolerability, or interpretation of efficacy or safety assessments from the applicable washout period prior to the Baseline / Randomisation until completion of the 1-hour post-procedure pain assessments.
4. Use of cannabis, cannabis-derived products, cannabinoid-containing products, synthetic cannabinoids, medicinal cannabis, cannabidiol (CBD), or tetrahydrocannabinol (THC)-containing products within 7 days prior to the Baseline / Randomisation and during the study.
5. Current or recent use of recreational, psychedelic, hallucinogenic, or illicit psychoactive substances, including but not limited to psilocybin, lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD), 3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA), non-prescribed ketamine, illicit or non-prescribed synthetic cannabinoids, or other psychoactive drugs, within 30 days prior to the Baseline / Randomisation and during the study.
6. Smoking, vaping, or use of nicotine-containing products is not exclusionary per se. However, participants who are unwilling or unable to comply with protocol-defined restrictions on smoking, vaping, or nicotine use from at least 1 hour prior to the pre-procedure pain assessment until completion of the 1-hour post-procedure pain assessment should be excluded.
7. Consumption of any alcoholic product within 24 hours prior to the Baseline / Randomisation and until completion of the 1-hour post-procedure assessment.
8. History of relevant neurological and/or psychiatric diseases/disorders that, in the Investigator’s opinion, may interfere with pain assessment, participant safety, or protocol compliance, including but not limited to epilepsy, severe anxiety disorders, or clinically relevant altered pain perception.
9. Clinically relevant hepatic impairment or any other condition that, in the Investigator’s opinion, may substantially impair lidocaine clearance or increase the risk of systemic lidocaine toxicity.
10. Body mass index (BMI) ≥40.0 kg/m2.
11. If WOCBP, positive pregnancy test.
12. Current use of anticoagulants that cannot be safely paused according to local clinical practice or that, in the Investigator’s opinion, may increase the risk of procedure-related bleeding.
13. If woman, she is breast-feeding or <6 weeks postpartum.
14. Known to be or suspected of being unable to comply with the CSP.
15. Incapacity and/or other circumstances rendering the patient unable to understand the nature, scope, and possible impact of the clinical study.
16. Any condition that, in the opinion of the Investigator, is likely to unfavourably alter the risk-benefit of study participation, confound interpretation of efficacy or safety results, or interfere with the satisfactory completion of the study requirements.
17. Participation in any clinical study within 30 days prior to Visit 1 or 5 times the elimination half-life of the investigational product received in the previous study, whichever period is longer.
18. Patient, who is a member of the Investigator site, Sponsor or clinical research organization staff, or an immediate relative.
19. Known hypersensitivity/allergic reaction to the other active substances (chlorhexidine, methyl-4-hydroxybenzoate, and propyl-4-hydroxybenzoate) or any of the excipients (hyetellose, propylene glycol, and sodium hydroxide) of the investigational products.
20. History of porphyria, glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency, or methaemoglobinaemia.
21. History of urethral syndrome or bladder pain syndrome.
22. History of severe disorders of the heart’s conduction system (e.g., bradycardia, atrial fibrillation, atrioventricular block, heart failure).
23. Presence of pelvic tumours that prevent or complicate the procedure.
24. Known active or clinically relevant recurrent urinary tract infections that, in the Investigator’s opinion, may interfere with the study assessments or participant safety.
25. Known defects in mucosal surfaces including periurethral abrasions, ulcerations, or lacerations.
